§1 — Pre-register the test

The demonstration is a prediction made before the comparison is seen. Write down, before the converter model is fitted, what the prediction must achieve and on which data. The predicted quantities are the coil-voltage lines at 6f, 12f, 18f, 24f and 30f, for three cases:

  • The EF5 and EF2 idle windows of the 2023 ±1 kV tests (E100865, E100863).
  • The ±2 kV tests (E100866 and the EF2 counterpart).
  • Their swing periods.

Set the tolerance per line, a band in decibels, and the aggregate criterion. Name the cases that are reported but not judged. EF6 is the obvious one until its 2023 filter state is known.

The criteria, set on 2026-10-13 before any model parameter was fitted:

QuantityHow it is measured, on model and data alikeBand
Coil-voltage lines at 6f, 12f, 18f, 24f, 30fmeasurement.measure of MMSYS/vol<coil> over the window, each line at its own fitted frequency (line_frequencies_hz); the model's output is passed through the booster-converter-model §3 measurement chain first. Amended 2026-10-13 at aecc62f, before any 2023 prediction was computed: the original single lock on the 12f line was biased when that line faded within the window (booster-converter-model §7).Within 3 dB of the measured line, or within 5 V where the measured line is below 10 V
Peak-to-peak ripplePeak-to-peak of the sum of the per-family folds, each source family (booster lines and base lines) folded at its own fitted frequency over the window (about 150 supply cycles), through the same chain. Amended with the line row, same reason.Within 3 dB of the measured value
Phase of each coil-voltage line at 6f, 12f, 18f, 24f, 30fNo recorded channel gives the supply phase, so the model's waveform, through the same chain, is shifted by the one supply phase θ that minimises its squared difference from the recorded samples (fold.fit_supply_phase). θ is the only quantity fitted to the data. Every line is a multiple of 6f, so θ is defined modulo 60°, and the criterion tests the lines' phases relative to one another. Each line's complex coefficient is estimated over four supply cycles, jointly with the line (66 − n)f that 4 kHz sampling folds about 33 Hz below it. The phase error is the shifted model coefficient's phase less the measured one. The judged value is the median over the consecutive four-cycle windows of the case's window, with the model evaluated at each window's operating point. Amended 2026-10-13 by the lead's decision, before any 2023 prediction was computed: on the idle windows of E100307, E100310, E100318 and E100321, the frozen 2021 model meets the amplitude bands at 6f and 18f, yet the phase-aligned overlay (booster-converter-model, bcm-overlay) puts its 18f, 24f and 30f phases more than 100° from the measured ones.Within 30° of the measured phase. A line whose measured amplitude is below 10 V is reported, not judged.

Aggregate: the prediction passes only if every judged quantity in every judged case lies inside its band. One miss fails the prediction, and §5 owes it an explanation. The same bands judge the held-out 2021 cases in booster-converter-model §5, for the 6f–24f lines, their phases and the peak-to-peak ripple.

§2 — The filter and grounding as fixed components

Extend power_convertor.filter_network into the full booster loop. The pieces are:

  • the base supply in series, as a second ripple source: the shot inventory in jt60sa-booster-ripple-evidence shows the coils carrying these lines with no booster current: about 130 V at 12f on EF2–EF5 and 310–390 V at 6f on CS1–4, EF1 and EF6. On the booster coils, which have the filter, the lines are as large as on the coils without one, so the data show the filter not acting on them. The network takes the base supply's voltage as a source input; its converter is a twelve-pulse configuration of the bridge pair in src/power_convertor/bridge.py (booster-converter-model §2), never a second converter model;
  • the booster with its series inductor;
  • the damped filter branch across the booster;
  • the coil, with its self- and mutual inductances as inputs (design values by default; the values booster-converter-model §4 identifies are applied in §4 below);
  • the Alternative Grounding System's mid-point resistors to ground.

Every component value is a design value with its source cited in the module docstring. None is fitted.

Done when the loop's coil-to-converter response reduces to the existing BoosterFilter.transfer when the grounding resistors are removed. Its common-mode path shows the coil terminals at about ± half the converter voltage to ground with the resistors present and at 0 and the full voltage without them; that pair is the negative control. Tests for both are in tests/test_filter_network.py.

§3 — Encode the 2023 converter structure from documents

Every coil carries two sources on the same supply frequency: the booster, seen through the filter, and the base supply, which the filter does not touch. The shot inventory (jt60sa-booster-ripple-evidence §9) shows the 2023 even lines on EF2 and EF5 are the twelve-pulse base supplies' ripple, not a booster run as a twelve-pulse pair, and the large 6f line on EF1 and EF6 is the other base-supply family's. The structure of each comes from documents, not from the 2023 data: the booster's from jt60sa-power-supply-sources §2 and the base supplies' from its §7. Encode both as configurations of the bridge pair that booster-converter-model §2 provides. The configuration fixes structure only: bridge count, connection and phase shift. The 2021-fitted bridge parameters are applied to it in §4, and it adds no parameter of its own. Two documented mechanisms are outside what one shared-angle series pair can express: the booster's separate firing angles and the base's signed parallel modules. Their owners are booster-converter-model §8 for the base modules and §9 for the booster pair, which extend the bridge library; §4 consumes them only after both land (gates g-fgp-7 and g-fgp-8).

Done when the 2023 configuration is a named, cited configuration in code. The plan records the document that fixes each structural choice. A configuration whose structure is unsupported by any document is marked as a hypothesis and reported separately from the judged prediction. Negative control: removing the citation from one structural choice moves that configuration out of the judged set and into the reported hypotheses, shown by a test. Clarified 2026-10-13 with the §1 amendment, before any 2023 prediction was computed: in this section, "judged" and "hypothesis" classify a configuration's documentary support, as configurations.partition_by_evidence computes it, and the control and its test stand unchanged. They no longer decide which cases the prediction scores. Under §1, a case resting on a hypothesis configuration is still judged, and its verdict names that hypothesis, so §4 runs this control to show that the demoted choice joins the hypotheses named beside the verdict. Where the documents and the data disagree, the documented structure is the judged one. Where documents disagree among themselves, the lead's ranking decides: a document describing the installed state ranks above a procurement drawing, which ranks above a simulator model. The ranking is a property of the documents, applied without reference to the data. The filter's shunt attachment (§6) is the first such case. Shirai et al., Nucl. Fusion 64 (2024) 112008, Fig. 9 and §3.3, describes the installed modification with the filter in parallel with the booster only. That outranks the MECS v2.9.2 procurement scheme (Fig 2.7-20) and its p. 9 simulator network, which put the shunt across base and booster. So the booster-only attachment is judged, and the drawn one is reported as the conflicting document.

§4 — Predict 2023 and compare

Run the 2021-fitted model with the documented 2023 structure, the design filter, the grounding, the 2023 operating point (measured reference and coil current) and the measured supply frequency. Compare with the 2023 coil-voltage lines and peak-to-peak ripple through the same measurement chain, using the library measurement that booster-converter-model §3 lifts out of scripts/figures/jt60sa_booster_ripple.py. The overlay figure extends that script's fig_lines() with the model's output rather than drawing a second one. The scoring entry point also computes §1's phase row. For each consecutive four-cycle window of a judged case it evaluates the model at that window's operating point and fits one supply phase with fold.fit_supply_phase. It estimates each measured line jointly with its folded (66 − n)f neighbour and takes the median phase error per line. Lift the joint line fit and the steady-state acquisition sampler that scripts/figures/booster_model_overlay.py carries into measurement.py and supply.py, and call those, rather than writing a third copy. Report three ablations beside the full prediction:

  • filter only, on the 2021 structure;
  • filter and structure, at the 2021 operating point;
  • everything.

Done when the prediction is scored against every judged case under the §1 criteria, with the verdict recorded whether it passes or not. Every judged line carries its amplitude error and its median phase error, and the aggregate counts both. One scoring entry point applies §3's judged-or-hypothesis status: every judged case lists, beside its verdict, the hypothesis choices its configurations rest on, as §1 now requires. The §3 citation-removal control is run through that entry point, to show that a demoted choice joins the list. EF6, report-only under §3, stays out of the judged aggregate. A figure in docs/figures/filter-grounding-prediction/ overlays predicted and measured lines per coil. The filter-only ablation, already known to miss the 12f and 24f lines by 6–11 times (12 V against 102 V and 3.3 V against 37 V for EF5; 22 V against 135 V and 6.3 V against 42 V for EF2), is shown failing the same criteria, which confirms the criteria can fail.

§5 — Explain what the prediction misses

Account for each residual the §4 comparison leaves. The EF6 anomaly that motivated this section is answered: its 2023 6f line is the base supply's own (research §9), not a failed trap. What remains open on EF1 and EF6 is the filtered booster residual itself, about 25 V expected under a base line near 300 V at 6f, which needs a phase-resolved two-source fit or a channel at the booster terminals (jt60sa-power-supply-sources §6). On EF2 and EF5 the 6f and 18f lines carry the filtered booster almost alone, because a twelve-pulse base cancels them. The 12f and 24f lines carry mostly the base supply. 30f is a twelve-pulse-cancelled order like 6f and 18f. A base contribution there, suggested by 2.3 V in E100303, which sits within the 1–3 V noise floor, and by EF2's 5.9 V against 2.4 V from the 2021 × design-filter estimate, is a hypothesis until a booster-free control shows a significant 30f line and its dependence on operating point. A residual is attributed by the family of lines it sits on. Test the candidate explanations against the data, not by refitting the prediction:

  • a detuned or disconnected filter;
  • a different bridge configuration, booster or base;
  • a different operating point: the base supplies' 12f and 24f lines change with coil current.

Done when every residual larger than the §1 tolerance has an explanation that is tested. For each residual, at least one candidate explanation has been run against a second shot or checked against a document, and the outcome recorded as confirmed or ruled out. A residual is left open only after such a test proved inconclusive, with the data that would decide it named. Negative control: a deliberately wrong attribution, a 12f residual on EF5 assigned to the booster or a 6f residual assigned to the base, is run through the same procedure and must be ruled out by its second-shot or line-family test.

Amended 2026-10-14: the swing-window residuals rest on a 12f line that measure_window could not lock below a 60.95 Hz fundamental. §8 re-judges those windows. This section takes its residual inventory from §8's corrected comparison, not from §4's, and no node is dispatched on it until §8 lands.

§6 — Where the filter's shunt attaches: drawings against data

The drawings and the data disagree about where the filter's shunt branch attaches. The procurement scheme (MECS v2.9.2 p. 8, Figure 2.7-20) and the Simulink network (p. 9) put the shunt (the limiting inductor, then the filter capacitor in parallel with the damping branch) between the booster output and the base supply's negative rail. That places it across base and booster in series, ahead of the QPC and the coil. With the booster bypass closed it sits directly across the base supply. That attachment filters the base supply's ripple too: with 4.45 mH in series, |H| is about 0.03 at 12f, and 0.28–0.44 with the bypass closed. The data show no such filtering. EF5 carries 102 V at 12f in E100865 and 129 V in E101088, against 128–130 V on EF3 and EF4, which have no filter. EF1 and EF6 carry 314 and 337 V at 6f, against 328–388 V on the CS coils. The open item is open-shunt-attachment.

Make the attachment a configuration of the loop that power_convertor.filter_network owns, beside the booster-only attachment §2 builds: as drawn (across base and booster, bypass open or closed) and booster only. Cite each value from the evidence document's source table: base-supply inductance 0.35 mH, or 0.175 mH in dual mode (p. 9); booster inductance 3.25 mH in Table 2.7-18 (p. 8) and 4.1 mH in the p. 9 model, carried as two named values; the grounding resistors (2 kΩ × 2 across the coil, 45 kΩ × 2 from the base–booster junction) and the 0.6 µF screen capacitance (p. 9). Which attachment is judged is set by §3's document ranking: the installed modification in Shirai et al. 2024 (Fig. 9) gives booster only, which is judged, and the MECS drawing is reported as the conflicting document.

Done when tests/test_filter_network.py shows the base-supply path attenuated to about 0.03 at 12f with the shunt as drawn and the bypass open, to 0.28–0.44 with the bypass closed, and passed near unity with the booster-only attachment. The booster path must be the same in both attachments when the base source is zero. The evidence fragment sets the measured EF5 and EF2 12f lines against EF3 and EF4 beside the two attachments' predictions, stating which one the data support. Negative control: a test that swaps the two attachments' labels must fail the base-path check.

§7 — Coil terminal voltage to ground

The lead's headline quantity is the peak-to-peak ripple because quench detection and the terminal insulation's Paschen margin see it, and the insulation sees each coil terminal's voltage to ground, not the voltage across the coil. The grounding system as installed (Shirai et al. 2024, Fig. 9; MECS v2.9.2 p. 9) has a 2.0 kΩ × 2 pair across the coil terminals with its midpoint grounded, a 45 kΩ × 2 pair on the supply side (raised from 2.5 kΩ), and a 0.6 µF screen capacitance. §6 declared the supply-side legs and the screen but left them out of every calculation. Bring them into GroundingSystem's common-mode path. Then predict each coil terminal's ripple voltage to ground, for the 2021 grounding (single-ended, before the system) and the installed 2023 grounding, on the same converter waveform.

Done when tests/test_filter_network.py shows the terminal-to-ground ripple at 6f and 12f changing with the 45 kΩ legs and the screen capacitance present, against their removal: the negative control is that removing them leaves the result unchanged, which must fail. The evidence fragment tabulates, for EF5 and EF2 at the 2021 and 2023 operating points, the predicted peak-to-peak terminal-to-ground ripple beside the coil-voltage peak-to-peak, so the Paschen-relevant number is stated next to the measured one.

§8 — Re-judge the 2023 swing windows at their own 12f

§4's 2023 swing windows (E100863–E100866, 7.53–8.53 s) run at about 60.86 Hz. Before booster-converter-model §20, measure_window could not lock 12f at that fundamental. A per-order frequency scan of the held traces reads their coil 12f at 130–147 V, where §4's measurement read 25–37 V. §4's finding that the model's 12f and peak-to-peak are about 10 dB too strong on those windows therefore rests on the mis-lock. The family-folded peak-to-peak used the same 12f frequency. So did the model's synthesis frequency, the four-cycle joint line coefficients and the fitted supply phase in prediction.py. A measured fundamental of 60.970–60.984 Hz against a true 60.852–60.864 Hz walks the 24f phasor by about 69° and the 6f phasor by about 17° over one four-cycle window, so the swing windows' 24f phase misses are suspect as well. The 2023 idle windows, at about 61.17 Hz, are unaffected.

Done when §4's judged 2023 cases are re-measured through measure_window as booster-converter-model §20 leaves it, and re-judged under §1's pre-registered criteria, in phase as well as in amplitude and peak-to-peak. The parameters frozen at 8ebe9b3 stay unchanged, and no ablation is added. The fragment states the re-judged verdict per case beside §4's landed verdict, which stays on the record as judged. Negative control: the fixed 61.2 Hz seeding reproduces §4's landed values.

§ Decisions

What tolerance per harmonic line counts as a successful prediction?

The lines span three decades, from about 1 kV at 6f in 2021 to a few volts at 18f in 2023, and the 2023 lines near 5 V sit close to the spectral noise floor of 1–3 V. A tolerance in decibels treats every decade alike; an absolute floor stops the smallest lines from deciding the verdict on noise. The filter-only ablation misses 12f and 24f by 12–20 dB, so the tolerance must be tighter than that to discriminate.

The lead chose the tighter band: a pass within 3 dB is stronger evidence that the circuit model, not its fitted constants, carries the prediction. The filter-only ablation misses the 12f and 24f lines by 16–21 dB (12 V against 102 V and 3.3 V against 37 V for EF5; 22 V against 135 V and 6.3 V against 42 V for EF2), so it falls 13–18 dB outside the band. The aggregate rule, also the lead's, is that every judged line must pass. The same band judges the held-out 2021 cases in booster-converter-model §5.

When documents disagree about the 2023 structure, which one sets the judged structure?

The MECS v2.9.2 procurement scheme (Fig 2.7-20) and its p. 9 simulator network put the filter's shunt across base and booster in series. Shirai et al., Nucl. Fusion 64 (2024) 112008, Fig. 9, labelled as the installed modification, puts it across the booster only.

The ranking is a property of the documents and is applied without reference to the data, so the prediction stays a test. For the shunt it makes the installed booster-only attachment the judged structure and the MECS drawing a reported alternative. Nothing is fitted on 2023 under either choice.
